title: Top View of a Binary Tree
statement:
You are given a binary tree. Imagine looking at it from directly above and report which nodes you can see.

Give every node a **horizontal position**: the root has position `0`, the left child of a node at position `p` has position `p - 1`, and its right child has position `p + 1`. Several nodes may share a position, but only one of them is visible from above:

- the node **closest to the root** (smallest depth) is visible;
- if two nodes share a position and have the same depth, the one that comes first in level order (the one further to the left) is visible.

Print the values of the visible nodes ordered by position from the smallest position (leftmost) to the largest (rightmost). Each occupied position contributes exactly one value.
inputFormat: A single line with the tree in level order: the root first, then for each node in that order its left child and its right child, using `null` for a missing child. Children of `null` entries are not listed, and trailing `null` values may be omitted. Tokens are separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print the values of the visible nodes, from the leftmost position to the rightmost, separated by single spaces.
constraints: The depth of the tree (nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path) is at most 5000

examples.explanation: Node 1 is at position 0, node 2 at -1, node 3 at 1, node 4 at -2 and node 5 at 2. Node 6 is the right child of node 4, so it sits at position -1, directly behind node 2, which is closer to the root. The visible nodes by position -2..2 are 4, 2, 1, 3, 5.
Node 4 is the left child of node 3, so its position is 0, the same as the root. The root is closer, so 4 is hidden. Node 5 is at position 2. Positions -1, 0, 1, 2 show 2, 1, 3, 5.
The tree is a chain going left: 1 at position 0, 2 at -1, 3 at -2, so every node is visible.

tests.input: 1 -3 null null 6 -8 null null 6 -7 null null -5 -8 null null 1 7 null null -3 -7 null null -2
5 null -7 1 9 -3 -7 null null -8 7 -3 9 -3 5 null null null null null null null 5
-9 null 8 3 3 null null 8 -5 null 7 null 0 3 -4 6 null null -4 null null null null null 3 -3

hints: Assign a horizontal position to every node: the root is 0, a left child is one less than its parent, a right child is one more.
Visit the nodes in level order. The first node you see at a given position is the visible one, because shallower nodes come first and, within a level, left comes before right.
Keep a map from position to the first value seen. At the end, output the values sorted by position (or track the minimum and maximum position and walk between them).
